Hegar sign and pigmentation are probable, and a positive serum test/fetal detection is positive/probable. Per Myles Textbook for Midwives. 146. Which of the following would be a disadvantage of breastfeeding? A. Involution occurs more rapidly B. The incidence of allergies increases due to maternal antibodies C. Which of the following would cause a false-positive result on a pregnancy test? A. The test was performed less than 10 days after an abortion B. Prolonged storage or wrong timing typically cause false negatives, and impending abortion is not a false positive. Per standard laboratory/midwifery references. 148. A client LMP began July 5, 2020. Which of the following danger signs should be reported promptly during the antepartum period? A. Constipation B. Breast tenderness C. Nasal stuffiness D. Leaking amniotic fluid Answer: D. Which of the following characteristics of contractions would the nurse expect to find in a client experiencing true labor? A. Occurring at irregular intervals B. Starting mainly in the abdomen C. Gradually increasing intervals D. Increasing intensity with walking Answer: D. Increasing intensity with walking Rationale: Myles Textbook for Midwives: true labour contractions are regular, begin in the back radiating to the abdomen, come at shortening intervals and intensify with activity/walking, unlike false labour which eases with walking. 151. During which of the following stages of labor would the nurse assess “crowning”? A. First stage B. Second stage C. Third stage D. Fourth stage Answer: B. Second stage Rationale: Crowning (the fetal head remaining visible at the vulva between contractions) occurs in the second stage of labour, the stage of expulsion (Myles Textbook for Midwives). 152. Which of the following nursing interventions would the nurse perform during the third stage of labor? A. Obtain a urine specimen and other laboratory tests B. Assess uterine contractions every 30 minutes C. Coach for effective client pushing D. Promote parent-newborn interaction Answer: D. Promote parent-newborn interaction Rationale: The third stage runs from birth of the baby to delivery of the placenta; while awaiting placental separation the nurse promotes early parent-newborn bonding/interaction. Pushing coaching is second stage (Myles Textbook for Midwives). 153. Which of the following actions demonstrates the nurse’s understanding of the newborn’s thermoregulatory ability? A. The other actions relate to airway, scoring and cord, not thermoregulation. 154. Immediately before expulsion, which of the following cardinal movements occur? A. Descent B. Flexion C. Extension D. Before birth, which of the following structures connects the right and left auricles of the heart? A. Umbilical vein B. Foramen ovale C. Ductus arteriosus D. Ductus venosus Answer: B. Foramen ovale Rationale: The foramen ovale is the fetal shunt in the interatrial septum allowing blood to pass from the right to the left atrium (auricles) bypassing the lungs. The ductus arteriosus links pulmonary artery to aorta (Anatomy & Physiology; fetal circulation). 156. When assessing the newborn’s heart rate, which of the following ranges would be considered normal if the newborn were sleeping? A. 80 beats per minute B. 100 beats per minute C. 120 beats per minute D. 140 beats per minute Answer: B. 100 beats per minute Rationale: Normal newborn heart rate is 120-160 bpm awake but may drop to about 100 bpm during sleep, which remains within normal limits (Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols; newborn assessment). 157. Which of the following is true regarding the fontanels of the newborn? A. The anterior is triangular shaped; the posterior is diamond-shaped B. Option C is correct; option A reverses the shapes (Myles/newborn assessment). 158. Which of the following groups of newborn reflexes below are present at birth and remain unchanged through adulthood? Rooting and stepping are primitive reflexes that disappear in infancy, excluding the other options (Kozier & Erb / newborn assessment). 159. Which of the following describes the Babinski reflex? A. The newborn’s toes will hyperextend and fan apart from the dorsiflexion of the big toe when one side of the foot is stroked upward from the ball of the heel and across the ball of the foot. Rationale: Babinski reflex: stroking the sole causes dorsiflexion of the big toe with fanning of the toes. Option B describes Moro, C describes rooting, D describes the crawl reflex (newborn reflex assessment). 160. Which of the following statements best describes hyperemesis gravidarum? A. In which of the following types of spontaneous abortions would the nurse assess dark brown vaginal discharge and a negative pregnancy test? A. Threatened B. Imminent C. Missed D. Incomplete Answer: C. Missed Rationale: In a missed abortion the fetus dies but is retained; the woman has a dark brown discharge and, as hormone levels fall, the pregnancy test becomes negative. Which of the following is described as premature separation of a normally implanted placenta during the second half of pregnancy, usually with severe hemorrhage? A. Placenta previa B. Which of the following is the nurse’s initial action when umbilical cord prolapse occurs? A. Begin monitoring maternal vital signs and FHR B. Place the client in a knee-chest position in bed C. For the client who is using oral contraceptives, the nurse informs the client about the need to take the pill at the same time each day to accomplish which of the following? A. A client in her third trimester tells the nurse, “I’m constipated all the time!” Which of the following should the nurse recommend? A. Daily enemas B. Laxatives C. Increased fiber intake D. Before assessing the postpartum client’s uterus for firmness and position in relation to the umbilicus and midline, which of the following should the nurse do first? A. Assess the vital signs B. The hormone responsible for the regeneration and proliferation of the endothelium during each menstrual cycle, after menstruation has taken place is: A. Progesterone B. Estrogen C. Estradiol D. While evaluating urine output for a mother in shock, the midwife is concerned if the urine output is: A. < 30ml/h B. > 30ml/h C. < 150 ml/h D. > 150ml/h Answer: A. < 30ml/h Rationale: Per Kenya MNH guidelines and Myles, urine output below 30 ml/hour indicates inadequate renal perfusion and is a concerning sign of shock/hypovolaemia. 184. Which of the following sign may help a midwife diagnose shoulder dystocia in labour ward? A. The fetal head remains slightly stuck in the vagina B. The risks associated with prematurity include: A. Asphyxia, hypothermia, cerebral haemorrhage B. Infections, jaundice, genito-urinary malformations C. Infections, asphyxia, malformation of the gut D. During vacuum extraction procedure, the centre of the vacuum cup should be placed over which of the flexion point on the fetal head? A. Pathological jaundice as a result of increased haemolysis involves all the following except: A. G6PD deficiency B. ABO incompatibility C. Gilbert’s syndrome D. Bacterial septicaemia Answer: C. The following nursing diagnosis will be of priority for a neonate undergoing phototherapy: A. Deficient fluid volume B. Imbalanced nutrition less than body requirements C. Deficient fluid volume Rationale: Per Basic Paediatric Protocols and nursing care standards, phototherapy increases insensible water loss and stool water, so deficient fluid volume (risk of dehydration) is the priority; skin integrity and thermoregulation are managed but fluid loss is the leading concern. 202. Which one of the following will be a priority nursing intervention for a neonate with Hemorrhagic disease of the newborn? A. Administer vitamin K B. Inform the physician C. A type of spina bifida which comprises of the skin, meninges with or without CSF is: A. Meningocele B. Myelomeningocele C. Cyatica D. Occulta Answer: A. You are called to the delivery suite for a 39-week baby about to be born through thick meconium. One of following is your first step of management: A. Which one of the following will be a priority nursing diagnosis for a postdate baby? A. Risk for aspiration related to delayed swallowing reflex and meconium aspiration B. You explain to a mother that a newborn has 'caput' because there is a swelling on his head that: A. Is a light pink colour and located at the base of his hairline B. Radiation refers to: A. loss of heat through water evaporation from the baby B. loss of heat through the baby shivering C. loss of heat from the baby's surface to surrounding colder objects D. loss of heat to moving air or fluid around the baby Answer: C. loss of heat from the baby's surface to surrounding colder objects Rationale: Radiation is heat transfer from the newborn's body surface to nearby cooler solid objects not in direct contact (e.g. cold walls/windows). Evaporation is water loss, convection is loss to moving air, conduction is loss to objects in contact. Per Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols / Myles (thermoregulation). 219. Reassuring without assessing is unsafe. Per Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols (newborn care). 220. A mother delivers a baby who has an Apgar score of 0/1. The body and the extremities are pale Rationale: An Apgar of 0/1 indicates a severely depressed neonate; only the completely pale/absent colour (0 for colour, no cyanosis grading possible) fits. When a newborn baby is in contact with cold surfaces, heat loss occurs by; A. Evaporation B. Radiation C. Convection D. Conduction Answer: D. Characteristics of a normal infant at birth include: A. Weight 3.5kg, length 40 cm, sunken abdomen B. Lies in an attitude of flexion, vernix caseosa, his head half his size C. The nurse prepares to administer a phytonadione (vitamin K) injection to a newborn, which explanation should the nurse give to the mother concerning the medication? You are taking vital signs observations on a postpartum client who delivered a healthy newborn 4 hours ago. Her temperature is 100.2° F or 37.9 What is the priority nursing action? A. A negative Kernig’s sign B. Absence of nuchal rigidity C. A positive Brudzinski’s sign D. A Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15 Answer: C. A positive Brudzinski's sign indicates developing meningitis; a negative Kernig's, absent nuchal rigidity and a normal GCS of 15 would suggest NO meningitis. 386. A client with myasthenia gravis has become increasingly weaker. The health care provider prepares to identify whether the client is reacting to an overdose of the medication (cholinergic crisis) or an increasing severity of the disease (myasthenic crisis). An injection of edrophonium is administered. Which finding would indicate that the client is in a cholinergic crisis? A. No change in the condition B. Complaints of muscle spasms C. An improvement of the weakness D. A temporary worsening of the condition Answer: D. A temporary worsening of the condition Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, in the edrophonium (Tensilon) test, improvement of weakness indicates myasthenic crisis (needs more anticholinesterase), whereas temporary worsening of weakness indicates cholinergic crisis (already too much drug). Hence temporary worsening indicates cholinergic crisis. 387. The nurse is positioning the female client with increased intracranial pressure. Which of the following positions would the nurse avoid? A. Head midline B. Head turned to the side C. Neck in neutral position D. Head of bed elevated 30 to 45 degrees Answer: B. Head turned to the side Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, with increased ICP the head should be kept midline and neutral with the bed elevated 30–45 degrees to promote venous drainage; turning/rotating the head to the side obstructs jugular venous outflow and raises ICP, so it is the position to AVOID. 388. The nurse is caring for the male client who begins to experience seizure activity while in bed. Which of the following actions by the nurse would be contraindicated? A. Loosening restrictive clothing B. Restraining the client’s limbs C. Removing the pillow and raising padded side rails D. Positioning the client to side, if possible , with the head flexed forward Answer: B. Restraining the client’s limbs Rationale: Per Kozier & Erb's Fundamentals and Brunner & Suddarth, during a seizure the nurse must NOT restrain the limbs (risks fractures/injury). Correct actions are loosening clothing, removing the pillow and padding side rails, and side-lying with head flexed forward; restraining limbs is contraindicated. 389. A female client has experienced an episode of myasthenic crisis. The nurse would assess whether the client has precipitating factors such as: A. getting too little exercise B. taking excess medication - (will cause cholinergic crisis instead) C. omitting doses of medication D. increasing intake of fatty foods Answer: C. omitting doses of medication Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, myasthenic crisis is precipitated by under-medication (omitting/missing anticholinesterase doses), infection, stress or surgery. Excess medication causes cholinergic crisis; too little exercise and fatty foods are not precipitants. Thus omitting doses precipitates myasthenic crisis. 390. A male client is having a tonic-clonic seizures. What should the nurse do first? A. Elevate the head of the bed B. Restrain the client’s arms and legs C. Place a tongue blade in the client’s mouth D. Take measures to prevent injury Answer: D. Take measures to prevent injury Rationale: Per Kozier & Erb's and Brunner & Suddarth, the FIRST priority during a tonic-clonic seizure is to protect the client from injury (ease to the floor/side-lying, clear the area, cushion the head). Do not restrain limbs or insert a tongue blade; elevating the head is not the priority. Injury prevention/safety comes first. 391. The nurse is teaching the female client with myasthenia gravis about the prevention of myasthenic and cholinergic crises. The nurse tells the client that this is most effectively done by: A. Eating large, well-balanced meals B. Doing muscle -strengthening exercises C. Doing all chores early in the day while less fatigued D. Taking medications on time to maintain therapeutic blood levels Answer: D. Taking medications on time to maintain therapeutic blood levels Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, prevention of both myasthenic and cholinergic crises depends on taking anticholinesterase medication precisely on time to keep therapeutic blood levels. Large meals, muscle-strengthening exercise and doing all chores early are not effective preventive measures. 392. Which of the following neurotransmitters is known to be associated with sleep, mood and appetite? A. Acetylcholine B. Dopamine C. Serotonin D. GABA Answer: C. Serotonin Rationale: Per standard physiology (Brunner & Suddarth / Lewis) and psychiatric nursing texts, serotonin (5-HT) regulates sleep, mood and appetite. Acetylcholine (muscle/memory), dopamine (movement/reward) and GABA (inhibition) do not fit this triad; serotonin does. 393. The neurons of the motor pathway control: A. Stress reaction B. Organs and glands C. Involuntary muscles D. Voluntary muscles Answer: D. Voluntary muscles Rationale: Per anatomy & physiology texts, the motor (somatic) pathway carries efferent impulses controlling voluntary (skeletal) muscles. Involuntary muscles, organs and glands are controlled by the autonomic nervous system; hence voluntary muscles is correct. 394. The area of the brain which is involved in the understanding of meaning is: A. Broca’s area B. association areas C. Wernicke area D. Motor speech area Answer: C. Wernicke area Rationale: Per neuroanatomy (Brunner & Suddarth), Wernicke's area (posterior superior temporal lobe) is responsible for comprehension/understanding of language meaning. Broca's/motor speech area handles speech production; general association areas integrate information, but understanding of meaning is specifically Wernicke's area. 395. Parkinson’s disease , is caused by the degeneration of neurons in an area of the brain called the: A. Substantia nigra B. Basal ganglia C. Cerebellum D. Corpus callosum Answer: A. Substantia nigra Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, Parkinson's disease results from degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra, reducing dopamine. Although the basal ganglia circuit is affected, the primary site of neuronal degeneration is the substantia nigra. 396. The division of the nervous system which controls the involuntary muscles, organs, and glands is: A. Somatic nervous system B. Autonomic nervous system C. Central nervous system D. The motor pathway of the CNS Answer: B. Autonomic nervous system Rationale: Per anatomy & physiology texts, the autonomic nervous system controls involuntary muscles, organs and glands (via sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions). The somatic system controls voluntary muscle; the CNS is the integrating centre. Hence autonomic nervous system is correct. 397. A client is unconscious following a tonic-clonic seizure. What should the nurse do FIRST? A. Place the client in a side-lying position B. Check the pulse C. Administer Valium D. Place a tongue blade in the mouth (Never do this! Places client in danger!) Answer: A. Place the client in a side-lying position Rationale: Per Kozier & Erb's and Brunner & Suddarth, in the postictal unconscious client the FIRST action is to place them in a side-lying (recovery) position to maintain a patent airway and prevent aspiration. Never insert a tongue blade; pulse check and Valium are not the immediate priority over airway positioning. 398. The nurse enters the room as the client is beginning to have a tonic-clonic seizure. What action should the nurse implement first? A. Determine if the client is incontinent of urine or stool. B. Provide the client with privacy during the seizure. C. Note the first thing the client does in the seizure. D. Assess the size of the client’s pupils. Answer: C. Note the first thing the client does in the seizure. Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, once safety is ensured the nurse's key nursing action at seizure onset is accurate observation/documentation, beginning with noting the first thing the client does (onset/aura and initial movements), which aids diagnosis and localization. Checking incontinence, providing privacy and pupil size are secondary to observing the seizure's onset. ⚠ More than one defensible answer 399. The nurse is teaching a class on the prevention of cerebrovascular accidents. Which of the following risk factors should the nurse identify as the most important factor contributing to a stroke? A. Sedentary lifestyle B. Smoking C. Obesity D. Hypertension Answer: D. Hypertension Rationale: Per Kenya MOH NCD guidelines and Brunner & Suddarth, hypertension is the single most important MODIFIABLE risk factor for stroke (cerebrovascular accident). Smoking, obesity and sedentary lifestyle also contribute, but hypertension is the leading contributing factor. 400. The nurse is assessing a 37-year-old client diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse expect to find? A. Flaccid muscles B. Tremors at rest C. Absent deep tendon reflexes D. Vision changes Answer: D. Vision changes Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, multiple sclerosis classically presents with visual disturbances (optic neuritis, diplopia, blurred vision), along with spasticity, hyperreflexia and intention (not resting) tremor. Flaccid muscles, resting tremor and absent deep tendon reflexes are not typical of MS; vision changes are the expected finding. 401. If a male client experienced a cerebrovascular accident (CVA) that damaged the hypothalamus, the nurse would anticipate that the client has problems with: A. Thinking and reasoning B. Body temperature control C. Balance and equilibrium D. Visual acuity Answer: B. Body temperature control Rationale: The hypothalamus is the principal thermoregulatory centre (also controlling hunger, thirst, and neuroendocrine function). Damage impairs body temperature control. Thinking/reasoning is cortical (frontal), balance is cerebellar, and visual acuity is occipital/optic pathway (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 402. During recovery from a cerebrovascular accident (CVA), a female client is given nothing by mouth, to help prevent aspiration. To determine when the client is ready for a liquid diet, the nurse assesses the client’s swallowing ability once each shift. This assessment evaluates A. Cranial nerves III and V B. Cranial nerves IX and X C. Cranial nerves I and II D. Cranial nerves VI and VIII Answer: B. Cranial nerves IX and X Rationale: Swallowing (gag reflex) is mediated by the glossopharyngeal (IX) and vagus (X) nerves. Assessing swallowing ability tests these cranial nerves before advancing diet post-CVA (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 403. A male client is admitted with a cervical spine injury sustained during a diving accident. When planning this client’s care, the nurse should assign highest priority to which nursing diagnosis? A. Ineffective breathing pattern Rationale: A cervical (high) spinal cord injury threatens the diaphragm and respiratory muscles (C3-C5 innervate the diaphragm). Airway/breathing is the highest priority per ABC prioritisation; the other diagnoses are important but not immediately life-threatening (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 404. Demyelination is defined as; A. Loss of an axon in a neuron B. Loss of dendrites in a neuron C. Loss of protective sheath surrounding neurons D. Loss of connective tissue between neurons Answer: C. Loss of protective sheath surrounding neurons Rationale: Demyelination is the loss/destruction of the myelin sheath surrounding nerve fibres (as in multiple sclerosis), slowing nerve conduction (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 405. Failure of muscle coordination , including unsteady movements and staggering walk, due to disorders in the cerebellum is called? A. Anoxia B. Dyslexia C. Paraplegia D. Ataxia Answer: D. Ataxia Rationale: Ataxia is impaired muscle coordination causing unsteady, staggering gait, characteristically due to cerebellar dysfunction. Anoxia is oxygen lack, dyslexia is a reading disorder, and paraplegia is lower-limb paralysis (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 406. Which part of the brain regulates heartbeat, breathing and other vital functions? A. Grey matter B. Brain stem C. Occipital lobe D. White matter Answer: B. Brain stem Rationale: The brain stem (specifically the medulla oblongata) contains the cardiac, respiratory, and vasomotor centres regulating heartbeat, breathing and other vital functions (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 407. Common complications of spinal cord injury include each of the following EXCEPT? A. Pressure sores B. Deep vein thrombosis C. Diarrhoea D. Urinary Tract infections Answer: C. Constipation, not diarrhoea, results from neurogenic bowel; thus diarrhoea is the exception (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 408. Broca’s area is located in the A. Brain stem B. Frontal lobe C. Parietal lobe D. Temporal lobe Answer: B. Wernicke area is located in the A. Brain stem B. Parietal lobe C. Temporal lobe D. Frontal lobe Answer: C. Temporal lobe Rationale: Wernicke's area (receptive/sensory speech centre) is located in the posterior superior temporal lobe of the dominant hemisphere; damage causes receptive (fluent) aphasia (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). 410. The presence of ptosis suggests damage to cranial nerve: A. IV B. V C. III D. VII Answer: C. A 60-year-old man complains of extremely severe, sharp, shooting pain in his face. Hee describes the episodes as being “like a bolt of electricity”that is brought about by touching a specific area. Pupil constriction B. Acceleration of heart beat C. Stimulation of sweat glands D. Contraction of hair muscles Answer: A. Pupil constriction Rationale: Parasympathetic (rest-and-digest) stimulation causes pupil constriction (miosis), slows the heart, and reduces secretions. Acceleration of heart rate, sweating, and pilo-erection are sympathetic responses (Kozier & Erb's Fundamentals; Brunner & Suddarth's). 413. Which one of the following is NOT a probable sign of the second stage of labour? A. uterine contractions B. No cervix felt on vaginal examination C. Rupture of membranes D. Rupture of membranes can occur at any stage and is not a specific sign of second stage, so it is the exception (Myles Textbook for Midwives). 414. Fear of losing control Rationale: Crying out in pain with each contraction during transition reflects fear of losing control, a recognised psychological response requiring reassurance and support. It is not exhaustion, involuntary grunting (an urge to push), or Valsalva (Myles Textbook for Midwives). ⚠ More than one defensible answer 415. In which one of the following stages is the placenta delivered? A. Stage 1, latent phase B. Stage 1, active phase C. Stage2 D. Stage 3 Answer: D. Endogenous oxytocin is released from the: A. anterior pituitary gland B. cervix C. posterior pituitary gland D. uterus Answer: C. posterior pituitary gland Rationale: Oxytocin is synthesised in the hypothalamus and released (stored) from the posterior pituitary gland; it stimulates uterine contraction and milk ejection (Myles Textbook for Midwives; physiology texts). 421. The midwife is caring for a woman in labour. She determines that the woman is beginning the 2nd stage of labour when which of the following signs is noted? A. Regular contractions and ruptured membranes are not defining signs (Myles Textbook for Midwives). 422. Which of the following is true about congenital abnormalities? A. Which of the following is the most appropriate feature seen in symmetric growth retarded infant? A. Weight is depressed more than length or head circumference. B. A new born infant was delivered in your maternity unit an hour ago. The skin of this infant appears to be red, wrinkly with ribs visible under the skin. When was the infant probably born? A. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia D. Non-hodgkin disease Answer: A. Hodgkin’s disease Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, the Reed-Sternberg cell is the pathognomonic hallmark used to diagnose Hodgkin's lymphoma. It is absent in non-Hodgkin lymphoma and the leukemias. 501. Characteristics of 1st degree burns include:- A. Erythema and pain B. Chilling and dry wounds C. Healing by scaling, painless wounds D. Black appearance, painless wounds Answer: A. Erythema and pain Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, first-degree (superficial) burns involve only the epidermis and present with erythema, pain, and no blistering (e.g., sunburn). Painless black/leathery wounds (D) indicate full-thickness burns. 502. In rheumatoid arthritis, inflammation of the jounts begins in the:- A. Hip, ankle,elbow B. Feet, wrist, toes C. Shoulder, fingers, wrist D. Clavicle, hands, fingers D C Answer: B. Feet, wrist, toes Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, rheumatoid arthritis typically begins symmetrically in the small joints of the hands and feet—wrists, MCP/PIP joints, and toes—before affecting larger joints. 503. The main aim of escharotomy in treatment of full thickness burns is to:- A. Improve oxygenation of the burnt tissues B. Remove the dead tissues C. Allow underlying viable tissues to expand D. Reduce pain C C Answer: C. Allow underlying viable tissues to expand Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, escharotomy incises the constricting inelastic eschar of circumferential full-thickness burns to relieve pressure, allowing underlying tissue to expand and restoring circulation/ventilation. 504. Risk factors of osteoporosis include:- A. Lack of Vitamin D in diet, high estrogen levels in women B. Too much exposure to the sun, low testosterone levels in men C. Increase in age, late menopause D. Excessive alcohol consumption, early menopause D Answer: D. Excessive alcohol consumption, early menopause D Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, osteoporosis risk factors include excessive alcohol intake and early menopause (reduced estrogen). Low—not high—estrogen and adequate vitamin D/sun are protective, making A and B incorrect. 505. Rhesus factor is found in the cell membrane of the:- A. Lymphocytes B. Granulocytes C. Erythrocytes D. Globulins C C Answer: C. Erythrocytes Rationale: Per standard physiology (Brunner & Suddarth), the Rhesus (Rh) antigen is located on the cell membrane of red blood cells (erythrocytes), determining Rh-positive or Rh-negative blood type. 506. Atherosclerosis impedes coronary blood flow by the following mechanisms A. Plaques obstructs the vein B. Plaques obstruct the artery C. Blood clots from outside the vessel wall D. Hardened vessels dilate to allow the blood to flow through B B Answer: B. Plaques obstruct the artery Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, atherosclerosis is the accumulation of lipid plaques within the coronary arteries, narrowing the lumen and impeding arterial blood flow to the myocardium. 507. The hypogastric region of the abdominopelvic cavity is; A. Inferior to the umbilical region, medial to the right iliac region B. Lateral to the left iliac region, superior to the umbilical region C. Medial to the right iliac region, lateral to the umbilical region D. Superior to the umbilical region, medial to the right iliac region D A Answer: A. Inferior to the umbilical region, medial to the right iliac region Rationale: Per standard anatomy, the hypogastric (suprapubic) region lies inferior to the umbilical region and medial to the right and left iliac regions in the nine-region abdominopelvic scheme. 508. The most appropriate nursing action when a client begins to cough and has difficulty breathing during nasogastric tube insertion is; A. Inserting the tube quickly B. Pulling the tube back a little and wait until the respiratory distress subsides D D Answer: D. Pulling the tube back a little and wait until the respiratory distress subsides D D Rationale: Per Kozier & Erb's, coughing and dyspnea during NG insertion suggest the tube has entered the airway; the nurse should withdraw the tube slightly and pause until distress resolves before advancing again. The expected outcomes for a patient who has “potential for impaired gas exchange related to fluid overload” is; A. No shortness of breath, scaphoid abdomen. B. Respiratory rate less than 20breaths/min, skin colour normal. Rationale: Per Kozier & Erb's, expected outcomes for impaired gas exchange are measurable normal respiratory function: respiratory rate <20/min and normal (pink) skin colour indicating adequate oxygenation. Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, lumbar puncture is performed below the spinal cord's end (L1-L2), typically in the L3-L4 (or L4-L5) interspace to avoid cord injury. Thoracic sites (A, B) are unsafe. 512. In chronic bronchitis;- A. There is cough and sputum production for at least 3 months in 2 consecutive years. B. Alveolar wall destruction (B) describes emphysema. 513. The condition in which the eyeballs are not properly aligned with each other is referred to as; A. Astigmatism B. Strabismus C. Presbyopia D. Amblyopia Answer: B. Strabismus Rationale: Per standard ophthalmic nursing (Brunner & Suddarth), strabismus is misalignment of the eyes so that they do not point in the same direction. Astigmatism is refractive error, presbyopia is age-related near-vision loss, and amblyopia is 'lazy eye'. 514. When assessing a client with possible Cushing’s syndrome you would expect to find; A. Deposits of adipose tissue in the trunk Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, Cushing's syndrome (cortisol excess) causes central (truncal) obesity, moon face, and buffalo hump. Rationale: Per Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols and Brunner & Suddarth, the leading bacterial causes of acute otitis media are Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae (with Moraxella catarrhalis). 517. While hemorrhage and hypocalcemia are risks, airway patency takes priority. 519. immediately after esophageal surgery the priority nursing assessment concerns the client's A. incision B. respiration C. level of pain D. nasogastric tube Answer: B. respiration Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, following esophageal surgery (thoracic approach) the priority assessment is respiratory status/airway and breathing, as the surgery affects the chest and diaphragm and impairs ventilation. Airway/breathing precede pain and NG assessment. 520. The client presents to the clinic with a serum cholesterol of 275 mg/dL and is placed on rosuvastatin (Crestor). Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth pharmacology, statins such as rosuvastatin can cause myopathy/rhabdomyolysis; clients must report unexplained muscle pain or weakness promptly. The 6-month-old client with a ventral septal defect is receiving Digitalis for regulation of his heart rate. Which finding should be reported to the doctor? A. Blood pressure of 126/80 B. A client with vaginal cancer is being treated with a radioactive vaginal implant. The client’s husband asks the nurse if he can spend the night with his wife. The nurse should explain that: A. Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth's radiation-safety (time-distance-shielding) principles, visitors of a client with a sealed radioactive implant are restricted in time (about 30 minutes) and distance; overnight stays are unsafe due to radiation exposure. 530. The nurse is caring for a client hospitalized with a facial stroke. Which diet selection would be suited to the client? A. Roast beef sandwich, potato chips, pickle spear, iced tea B. The physician has prescribed Novolog insulin for a client with diabetes mellitus. Which statement indicates that the client knows when the peak action of the insulin occurs? The physician has prescribed Nexium (esomeprazole) for a client with erosive gastritis. The nurse should administer the medication: A. 30 minutes before meals B. With each meal C. When the nurse checks the fundus of a client on the first postpartum day, she notes that the fundus is firm, is at the level of the umbilicus, and is displaced to the right. The client with Alzheimer’s disease is being assisted with activities of daily living when the nurse notes that the client uses her toothbrush to brush her hair. The client has elected to have epidural anesthesia to relieve labor pain. If the client experiences hypotension, the nurse would: A. Place her in Trendelenburg position B. A 6-year-old client is admitted to the unit with a hemoglobin of 6g/dL. The physician has written an order to transfuse 2 units of whole blood. Which of the following outcome criteria would the nurse use? A. Body temperature of 37.2 celsius or less B. Toes moved in active range of motion C. Sensation reported when soles of feet are touched D. Capillary refill of < 3 seconds Answer: D. Capillary refill of < 3 seconds Rationale: In sickle cell anemia, monitoring peripheral circulation is best evaluated by capillary refill; a refill under 3 seconds is the outcome criterion indicating adequate lower-extremity perfusion (Brunner & Suddarth's, haematologic disorders). 558. A 30-year-old male from Haiti is brought to the emergency department in sickle cell crisis. What is the best position for this client? A. Side-lying with knees flexed B. Knee-chest C. High Fowler's with knees flexed D. Semi-Fowler's with legs extended on the bed Answer: D. Semi-Fowler's with legs extended on the bed Rationale: In sickle cell crisis, positions that flex joints and impede circulation are avoided; semi-Fowler's with legs extended promotes comfort, oxygenation and unrestricted circulation (Brunner & Suddarth's, sickle cell crisis management). 559. A 25-year-old male is admitted in sickle cell crisis. Which of the following interventions would be of highest priority for this client? A. Taking hourly blood pressures with mechanical cuff B. Encouraging fluid intake of at least 200mL per hour C. Position in high Fowler's with knee gatch raised D. Administering Tylenol as ordered Answer: B. Encouraging fluid intake of at least 200mL per hour Rationale: Hydration is the highest priority in sickle cell crisis because it reduces blood viscosity, promotes circulation and limits further sickling and vaso-occlusion (Brunner & Suddarth's, sickle cell crisis). 560. Which of the following foods would the nurse encourage the client in sickle cell crisis to eat? A. Peaches B. Cottage cheese C. Popsicle D. Lima beans Answer: C. Popsicle Rationale: Fluid intake is essential in sickle cell crisis; a popsicle provides additional fluids to support hydration and reduce sickling, making it the best choice to encourage (Brunner & Suddarth's, sickle cell crisis hydration). 561. A newly admitted client has sickle cell crisis. The nurse is planning care based on assessment of the client. The client is complaining of severe pain in his feet and hands. The pulse oximetry is 92. Which of the following interventions would be implemented first? Assume that there are orders for each intervention. A. Adjust the room temperature B. Give a bolus of IV fluids C. Start O2 D. Administer meperidine (Demerol) 75mg IV push Answer: C. Start O2 Rationale: With a pulse oximetry of 92 and vaso-occlusive pain, correcting hypoxia by starting oxygen is implemented first to reduce further sickling, following the ABC priority (Brunner & Suddarth's, sickle cell crisis oxygenation). 562. The nurse is instructing a client with iron-deficiency anemia. Which of the following meal plans would the nurse expect the client to select? A. Roast beef, gelatin salad, green beans, and peach pie B. Chicken salad sandwich, coleslaw, French fries, ice cream C. Egg salad on wheat bread, carrot sticks, lettuce salad, raisin pie D. Pork chop, creamed potatoes, corn, and coconut cake Answer: C. Egg salad on wheat bread, carrot sticks, lettuce salad, raisin pie Rationale: Iron-rich choices include eggs, whole wheat, leafy green vegetables and raisins (dried fruit); this meal provides the most dietary iron for iron-deficiency anemia (Kenya nutrition guidelines; Brunner & Suddarth's). 563. Clients with sickle cell anemia are taught to avoid activities that cause hypoxia and hypoxemia. Which of the following activities would the nurse recommend? A. A family vacation in the Rocky Mountains B. Chaperoning the local boys club on a snow-skiing trip C. Traveling by airplane for business trips D. A bus trip to the Museum of Natural History Answer: D. A bus trip to the Museum of Natural History Rationale: Activities causing hypoxia (high altitude in the Rocky Mountains, cold snow-skiing, unpressurised/altitude air travel) must be avoided; a low-altitude bus trip is safe (Brunner & Suddarth's, sickle cell patient education). 564. The nurse is conducting an admission assessment of a client with vitamin B12 deficiency. Which of the following would the nurse include in the physical assessment? A. Palpate the spleen B. Take the blood pressure C. Examine the feet for petechiae D. Examine the tongue Answer: D. Examine the tongue Rationale: Vitamin B12 deficiency characteristically causes glossitis (a smooth, beefy-red, sore tongue); examining the tongue is the relevant physical assessment finding (Brunner & Suddarth's, megaloblastic/pernicious anemia). 565. An African American female comes to the outpatient clinic. The physician suspects vitamin B12 deficiency anemia. Because jaundice is often a clinical manifestation of this type of anemia, what body part would be the best indicator? A. Conjunctiva of the eye B. Soles of the feet C. Roof of the mouth D. Shins Answer: C. Roof of the mouth Rationale: In dark-skinned clients jaundice is best detected in the hard palate (roof of the mouth) and sclera where the yellow discoloration is most visible (Kozier & Erb's, assessment of skin colour in dark-skinned clients). 566. The nurse is conducting a physical assessment on a client with anemia. Which of the following clinical manifestations would be most indicative of the anemia? A. BP 146/88 B. Respirations 28 shallow C. Weight gain of 10 pounds in 6 months D. Pink complexion Answer: B. Respirations 28 shallow Rationale: Anemia reduces oxygen-carrying capacity, causing compensatory tachypnea and dyspnea; increased shallow respirations (28) is the most indicative manifestation, while pink complexion would be inconsistent with anemia (Brunner & Suddarth's, anemia assessment). 567. A 33-year-old male is being evaluated for possible acute leukemia. Which of the following would the nurse inquire about as a part of the assessment? A. The client collects stamps as a hobby. B. The client recently lost his job as a postal worker. C. The client had radiation for treatment of Hodgkin's disease as a teenager. D. The client's brother had leukemia as a child. Answer: C. The client had radiation for treatment of Hodgkin's disease as a teenager. Rationale: Prior radiation therapy is a well-established risk factor for developing acute leukemia; this history is the relevant assessment inquiry (Brunner & Suddarth's, leukemia risk factors). 568. An African American client is admitted with acute leukemia. The nurse is assessing for signs and symptoms of bleeding. Where is the best site for examining for the presence of petechiae? A. The abdomen B. The thorax C. The earlobes D. The soles of the feet Answer: C. The earlobes Rationale: In dark-skinned clients petechiae are best assessed in areas of lighter pigmentation with thin skin such as the earlobes and oral mucosa/conjunctiva (Kozier & Erb's, skin assessment in dark-skinned clients). 569. Which of the following would be the priority nursing diagnosis for the adult client with acute leukemia? A. Oral mucous membrane, altered related to chemotherapy B. Risk for injury related to thrombocytopenia C. Fatigue related to the disease process D. Interrupted family processes related to life-threatening illness of a family member Answer: B. Risk for injury related to thrombocytopenia Rationale: In acute leukemia, thrombocytopenia predisposes to life-threatening hemorrhage; risk for injury/bleeding is the priority (physiologic safety) nursing diagnosis (Brunner & Suddarth's, leukemia nursing care). 570. A 21-year-old male with Hodgkin's lymphoma is a senior at the local university. He is engaged to be married and is to begin a new job upon graduation. Which of the following diagnoses would be a priority for this client? A. Sexual dysfunction related to radiation therapy B. Anticipatory grieving related to terminal illness C. Tissue integrity related to prolonged bed rest D. Fatigue related to chemotherapy Answer: A. Sexual dysfunction related to radiation therapy Rationale: Hodgkin's lymphoma is highly curable so anticipatory grieving for terminal illness is inappropriate; for a young engaged man, radiation-induced sexual dysfunction/infertility is the priority concern (Brunner & Suddarth's, Hodgkin's lymphoma). 571. The home health nurse is visiting a client with autoimmune thrombocytopenic purpura (ATP). The client's platelet count currently is 80, It will be most important to teach the client and family about: A. Bleeding precautions B. Prevention of falls C. Oxygen therapy D. Conservation of energy Answer: A. Bleeding precautions Rationale: With a low platelet count in ATP (ITP), the priority teaching is bleeding precautions to prevent hemorrhage (Brunner & Suddarth's, thrombocytopenia/ITP care). 572. A client with a pituitary tumor has had a transsphenoidal hypophysectomy. Which of the following interventions would be appropriate for this client? A. Place the client in Trendelenburg position for postural drainage B. Encourage coughing and deep breathing every 2 hours C. Elevate the head of the bed 30° D. Encourage the Valsalva maneuver for bowel movements Answer: C. Elevate the head of the bed 30° Rationale: After transsphenoidal hypophysectomy, the head of the bed is elevated 30° to reduce pressure on the sella and CSF leak risk; coughing, Valsalva and Trendelenburg increase intracranial pressure and are contraindicated (Brunner & Suddarth's, hypophysectomy care). 573. The client with a history of diabetes insipidus is admitted with polyuria, polydipsia, and mental confusion. The priority intervention for this client is: A. Measure the urinary output B. Check the vital signs C. Encourage increased fluid intake D. Weigh the client Answer: B. Check the vital signs Rationale: Diabetes insipidus with polyuria and confusion risks severe dehydration and hypovolemic shock; assessing vital signs is the priority to detect fluid volume/hemodynamic instability (Brunner & Suddarth's, diabetes insipidus). 574. A client with hemophilia has a nosebleed. Which nursing action is most appropriate to control the bleeding? A. Place the client in a sitting position with the head hyperextended B. Pack the nares tightly with gauze to apply pressure to the source of bleeding C. Pinch the soft lower part of the nose for a minimum of 5 minutes D. Apply ice packs to the forehead and back of the neck Answer: C. Pinch the soft lower part of the nose for a minimum of 5 minutes Rationale: For epistaxis in hemophilia, applying steady pressure by pinching the soft lower nose (with the client upright, head forward) controls bleeding; hyperextension and tight packing are avoided (Basic nursing/first aid; Brunner & Suddarth's, hemophilia). 575. A client has had a unilateral adrenalectomy to remove a tumor. To prevent complications, the most important measurement in the immediate postoperative period for the nurse to take is: A. Blood pressure B. Temperature C. Output D. Specific gravity Answer: A. Blood pressure Rationale: After adrenalectomy, adrenal hormone fluctuations cause hemodynamic instability (hypotension or hypertension); blood pressure is the most important immediate postoperative measurement (Brunner & Suddarth's, adrenal surgery). 576. A client with Addison's disease has been admitted with a history of nausea and vomiting for the past 3 days. The client is receiving IV glucocorticoids (Solu-Medrol). Which of the following interventions would the nurse implement? A. Glucometer readings as ordered B. Intake/output measurements C. Sodium and potassium levels monitored D. Daily weights Answer: C. Sodium and potassium levels monitored Rationale: In Addison's disease/adrenal insufficiency the key electrolyte disturbance is hyponatremia and hyperkalemia; monitoring sodium and potassium is the priority intervention (Brunner & Suddarth's, Addisonian crisis). 577. A client had a total thyroidectomy yesterday. The client is complaining of tingling around the mouth and in the fingers and toes. What would the nurses' next action be? A. Obtain a crash cart B. Check the calcium level C. Assess the dressing for drainage D. Assess the blood pressure for hypertension Answer: B. Check the calcium level Rationale: Tingling of the mouth, fingers and toes after thyroidectomy signals hypocalcemia from accidental parathyroid injury; the nurse should check the calcium level and watch for tetany (Brunner & Suddarth's, post-thyroidectomy complications). 578. A 32-year-old mother of three is brought to the clinic. Her pulse is 52, there is a weight gain of 30 pounds in 4 months, and the client is wearing two sweaters. The client is diagnosed with hypothyroidism. Which of the following nursing diagnoses is of highest priority? A. Impaired physical mobility related to decreased endurance B. Hypothermia r/t decreased metabolic rate C. Disturbed thought processes r/t interstitial edema D. Decreased cardiac output r/t bradycardia Answer: D. Decreased cardiac output r/t bradycardia Rationale: Using the airway/circulation priority, the pulse of 52 (bradycardia) makes decreased cardiac output the highest-priority (physiologic) diagnosis in hypothyroidism (Brunner & Suddarth's, hypothyroidism; Maslow/ABC prioritisation). 579. A primigravida, age 42, is 6 weeks pregnant. Based on the client's age, her infant is at risk for: A. Down syndrome B. Respiratory distress syndrome C. Turner's syndrome D. Pathological jaundice Answer: A. Down syndrome Rationale: Advanced maternal age (42) markedly increases the risk of chromosomal trisomies, most notably Down syndrome (trisomy 21) (Myles Textbook for Midwives; Kenya maternal care guidelines). 580. A client with a missed abortion at 29 weeks gestation is admitted to the hospital. The client will most likely be treated with: A. Magnesium sulfate B. Calcium gluconate C. Dinoprostone (Prostin E.) D. Bromocriptine (Pardel) Answer: C. Dinoprostone (Prostin E.) Rationale: A missed abortion at 29 weeks requires evacuation; dinoprostone (a prostaglandin E) is used to induce cervical ripening and uterine contractions to expel the retained products (Myles Textbook for Midwives; Kenya maternal guidelines on induction). 581. A client with preeclampsia has been receiving an infusion containing magnesium sulfate for a blood pressure that is 160/80; deep tendon reflexes are 1 plus, and the urinary output for the past hour is 100mL. The nurse should: A. Continue the infusion of magnesium sulfate while monitoring the client's blood pressure B. Stop the infusion of magnesium sulfate and contact the physician C. Slow the infusion rate and turn the client on her left side D. Administer calcium gluconate IV push and continue to monitor the blood pressure Answer: A. Continue the infusion of magnesium sulfate while monitoring the client's blood pressure Rationale: Per Kenya National Maternal guidelines/Myles, MgSO4 is withheld only for magnesium toxicity signs: respiratory depression, absent reflexes, or urine output <30mL/hr (<100mL/4hr). Here reflexes are present (1+) and output is adequate (100mL/hr), so the infusion is safely continued with monitoring. 582. Which statement made by the nurse describes the inheritance pattern of autosomal recessive disorders? A. An affected newborn has unaffected parents. B. An affected newborn has one affected parent. C. Affected parents have a one in four chance of passing on the defective gene. D. Affected parents have unaffected children who are carriers. Answer: A. An affected newborn has unaffected parents. Rationale: Per genetics (Brunner & Suddarth), in autosomal recessive inheritance both unaffected parents are typically heterozygous carriers, so an affected child is born to phenotypically unaffected parents. The 1-in-4 risk refers to two carrier (not affected) parents, making that option imprecise. 583. A pregnant client, age 32, asks the nurse why her doctor has recommended a serum alpha fetoprotein. The nurse should explain that the doctor has recommended the test: A. Because it is a state law B. To detect cardiovascular defects C. Because of her age D. To detect neurological defects Answer: D. To detect neurological defects Rationale: Per Myles/antenatal screening, maternal serum alpha-fetoprotein screens for neural tube (neurological) defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly; elevated AFP indicates open NTDs. Age relates to Down screening, not AFP alone. 584. A client with hypothyroidism asks the nurse if she will still need to take thyroid medication during the pregnancy. The nurse's response is based on the knowledge that: A. There is no need to take thyroid medication because the fetus's thyroid produces a thyroid-stimulating hormone. B. Regulation of thyroid medication is more difficult because the thyroid gland increases in size during pregnancy. C. It is more difficult to maintain thyroid regulation during pregnancy due to a slowing of metabolism. D. Fetal growth is arrested if thyroid medication is continued during pregnancy. Answer: B. Regulation of thyroid medication is more difficult because the thyroid gland increases in size during pregnancy. Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth/maternal endocrine physiology, thyroid demand and gland size increase in pregnancy so thyroid replacement often needs upward adjustment; medication must be continued, not stopped. Metabolism rises (not slows) in pregnancy. 585. The nurse is responsible for performing a neonatal assessment on a full-term infant. At 1 minute, the nurse would expect to find: A. An apical pulse of 100 B. An absence of tonus C. Cyanosis of the feet and hands D. Jaundice of the skin and sclera Answer: C. Cyanosis of the feet and hands Rationale: Per Basic Paediatric Protocols/newborn assessment, acrocyanosis (bluish hands and feet) is a normal finding at 1 minute due to peripheral circulation. Apical pulse should be 120-160, and jaundice at 1 minute is abnormal. 586. A client with sickle cell anemia is admitted to the labor and delivery unit during the first phase of labor. The nurse should anticipate the client's need for: A. Supplemental oxygen B. Fluid restriction C. Blood transfusion D. Delivery by Caesarean section Answer: A. Supplemental oxygen Rationale: Per Kenya haematology/maternal guidelines, in sickle cell disease during labor the priority is preventing hypoxia and sickling crisis, so supplemental oxygen and hydration are anticipated. Fluid restriction is contraindicated as it promotes sickling. 587. A client with diabetes has an order for ultrasonography. Preparation for an ultrasound includes: A. Increasing fluid intake B. Limiting ambulation C. Administering an enema D. Withholding food for 8 hours Answer: A. Increasing fluid intake Rationale: Per obstetric ultrasound preparation (Myles), a full bladder from increased fluid intake elevates the uterus and provides an acoustic window for imaging in pregnancy. Withholding food and enemas are not required for obstetric/abdominal ultrasound. 588. An infant who weighs 8 pounds at birth would be expected to weigh how many pounds at 1 year? A. 14 pounds B. 16 pounds C. 18 pounds D. 24 pounds Answer: D. 24 pounds Rationale: Per Basic Paediatric Protocols/growth norms, an infant's birth weight roughly triples by 1 year; 8 pounds x 3 = 24 pounds. Doubling occurs by ~5-6 months. 589. A pregnant client with a history of alcohol addiction is scheduled for a nonstress test. The nonstress test: A. Determines the lung maturity of the fetus B. Measures the activity of the fetus C. Shows the effect of contractions on the fetal heart rate D. Measures the neurological well-being of the fetus Answer: B. Measures the activity of the fetus Rationale: Per Myles antenatal testing, a nonstress test evaluates fetal heart rate accelerations in response to fetal movement (activity), reflecting well-being. Contraction effects are assessed by the contraction stress test, and lung maturity by L/S ratio. 590. A full-term male has hypospadias. Which statement describes hypospadias? A. The urethral opening is absent. B. The urethra opens on the dorsal side of the penis. C. The penis is shorter than usual. D. The urethra opens on the ventral side of the penis. Answer: D. The urethra opens on the ventral side of the penis. Rationale: Per Basic Paediatric Protocols/paediatric surgery, hypospadias is a congenital anomaly in which the urethral meatus opens on the ventral (underside) of the penis. A dorsal opening describes epispadias. 591. A gravida III, para II is admitted to the labor unit. Vaginal exam reveals that the client's cervix is 8cm dilated, with complete effacement. The priority nursing diagnosis at this time is: A. Alteration in coping related to pain B. Potential for injury related to precipitate delivery C. Alteration in elimination related to anesthesia D. Potential for fluid volume deficit related to NPO status Answer: B. Potential for injury related to precipitate delivery Rationale: Per Myles, a multipara (gravida III para II) at 8cm with complete effacement is in advanced active/transition labor and may deliver rapidly; the priority is preventing injury from precipitate delivery. Pain and elimination are lower priority than safety. 592. The client with varicella will most likely have an order for which category of medication? A. Antibiotics B. Antipyretics C. Antivirals D. Anticoagulants Answer: C. Antivirals Rationale: Per Kenya IMNCI/clinical guidelines, varicella (chickenpox) is a viral infection; antivirals such as acyclovir are indicated in severe or high-risk cases. Antibiotics treat only secondary bacterial infection. 593. A client is admitted complaining of chest pain. Which of the following drug orders should the nurse question? A. Nitroglycerin B. Ampicillin C. Propranolol D. Verapamil Answer: B. Ampicillin Rationale: Per Kenya EML/cardiac pharmacology, nitroglycerin, propranolol and verapamil are all appropriate for anginal chest pain; ampicillin is an antibiotic with no role in chest pain and should be questioned. 594. Which of the following instructions should be included in the teaching for the client with rheumatoid arthritis? A. Avoid exercise because it fatigues the joints. B. Take prescribed anti-inflammatory medications with meals. C. Alternate hot and cold packs to affected joints. D. Avoid weight-bearing activity. Answer: B. Take prescribed anti-inflammatory medications with meals. Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth, NSAIDs/anti-inflammatory drugs for rheumatoid arthritis should be taken with meals to reduce gastric irritation. Exercise (ROM) is encouraged, not avoided, so the other options are incorrect. 595. A client with acute pancreatitis is experiencing severe abdominal pain. Which of the following orders should be questioned by the nurse? A. Meperidine 100mg IM q 4 hours PRN pain B. Mylanta 30 ccs q 4 hours via NG C. Cimetidine 300mg PO q.i.d. D. Morphine 8mg IM q 4 hours PRN pain Rationale: Per traditional med-surg teaching (Brunner & Suddarth), morphine was avoided in acute pancreatitis due to concern for sphincter of Oddi spasm; meperidine was historically preferred, so the morphine order is the one questioned in NCK-style items. 596. During the assessment of a laboring client, the nurse notes that the FHT are loudest in the upper-right quadrant. The infant is most likely in which position? A. Right breech presentation B. Right occipital anterior presentation C. Left sacral anterior presentation D. Left occipital transverse presentation Answer: A. Right breech presentation Rationale: Per Myles, fetal heart tones heard loudest in the upper quadrant indicate the fetal back/heart is high in the uterus, consistent with a breech presentation; on the right side this is a right breech. Vertex presentations transmit FHTs in the lower quadrants. 597. The primary physiological alteration in the development of asthma is: A. Bronchiolar inflammation and dyspnea B. Hypersecretion of abnormally viscous mucus C. Infectious processes causing mucosal edema D. Spasm of bronchial smooth muscle Answer: D. Spasm of bronchial smooth muscle Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth respiratory pathophysiology, the primary reversible physiological alteration in asthma is bronchospasm (spasm of bronchial smooth muscle), accompanied by inflammation and mucus. Bronchospasm is the hallmark driving airway narrowing. 598. To maintain Bryant's traction, the nurse must make certain that the child's: A. Buttocks must clear the mattress. 599. The client has an order for a trough to be drawn on the client receiving Vancomycin. Levels drawn after infusion reflect peak, not trough. 600. The client using a diaphragm should be instructed to: A. Refrain from keeping the diaphragm in longer than 4 hours B. A 5-pound gain generally does not require refitting, and it must stay in at least 6 hours after intercourse. 601. The nurse is providing postpartum teaching for a mother planning to breastfeed her infant. Which of the client's statements indicates the need for additional teaching? A. "I'm wearing a support bra." B. "I'm expressing milk from my breast." C. "I'm drinking four glasses of fluid during a 24-hour period." D. "While I'm in the shower, I'll allow the water to run over my breasts." Answer: C. Rationale: Per Myles/postpartum lactation teaching, a breastfeeding mother needs increased fluids (about 8-10 glasses/day); only four glasses in 24 hours is inadequate and indicates a need for more teaching. Support bra, expressing milk, and letting water run over breasts are correct. 602. Damage to the VII cranial nerve results in: A. Facial pain B. Absence of ability to smell C. Absence of eye movement D. Tinnitus Answer: A. Facial pain Rationale: Per neuroanatomy (Brunner & Suddarth), the VII (facial) nerve controls facial muscle movement and taste; its damage causes facial weakness/paralysis and altered sensation. Smell is CN I, eye movement CN III/IV/VI, so facial involvement is the best fit among the options. ⚠ More than one defensible answer 603. A client is receiving Pyridium (phenazopyridine hydrochloride) for a urinary tract infection. The client should be taught that the medication may: A. Cause diarrhea B. Change the color of her urine C. Cause mental confusion D. Cause changes in taste Answer: B. Change the color of her urine Rationale: Per Kenya EML/pharmacology, phenazopyridine (Pyridium) is a urinary analgesic that characteristically turns urine reddish-orange; clients must be forewarned to avoid alarm and staining. It does not typically cause diarrhea or confusion. 604. Which of the following tests should be performed before beginning a prescription of Accutane? A. Check the calcium level B. Perform a pregnancy test C. Monitor apical pulse D. Obtain a creatinine level Answer: B. Perform a pregnancy test Rationale: Per pharmacology (Kenya EML/BNF), isotretinoin (Accutane) is highly teratogenic, so a negative pregnancy test is mandatory before starting therapy in women of childbearing potential. Calcium and creatinine are not the primary pre-treatment screens. 605. A client with AIDS is taking Zovirax (acyclovir). Which nursing intervention is most critical during the administration of acyclovir? A. Limit the client's activity B. Encourage a high-carbohydrate diet C. Activity limitation and spirometry are not priorities. 606. A client is admitted for an MRI. The nurse should question the client regarding: A. Pregnancy B. A titanium hip replacement C. Allergies to antibiotics D. Inability to move his feet Answer: B. A titanium hip replacement Rationale: Per diagnostic imaging safety (Brunner & Suddarth), MRI uses a strong magnetic field, so the nurse must screen for metal implants; ferromagnetic hardware is a contraindication. Screening for implants/metal is the key MRI safety concern among these options. 607. The nurse is caring for the client receiving Amphotericin B. Which of the following indicates that the client has experienced toxicity to this drug? A. Changes in vision B. Nausea C. Urinary frequency D. Changes in skin color Answer: B. Nausea Rationale: Per pharmacology (Brunner & Suddarth), amphotericin B commonly causes infusion reactions such as fever, chills, nausea and, importantly, nephrotoxicity; among the listed options nausea is the recognized adverse/toxic effect. Visual changes are not characteristic. ⚠ More than one defensible answer 608. The nurse should visit which of the following clients first? A. The client with diabetes with a blood glucose of 95mg/dL B. The client with hypertension being maintained on Lisinopril C. The client with chest pain and a history of angina D. The client with Raynaud's disease Answer: C. The client with chest pain and a history of angina Rationale: Per triage/prioritization (ABC, Brunner & Suddarth), the client with active chest pain and angina history is at risk of an evolving myocardial infarction and must be seen first. The others are stable with controlled findings. 609. A client with cystic fibrosis is taking pancreatic enzymes. The nurse should administer this medication: A. Once per day in the morning B. Three times per day with meals C. Once per day at bedtime D. Four times per day Answer: B. Three times per day with meals Rationale: Pancreatic enzyme replacements (pancrelipase) must be given with each meal and snack so the enzymes are present to digest fat, protein, and carbohydrate as food enters the gut (Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing). Giving them once daily would leave most meals without enzyme support. 610. Cataracts result in opacity of the crystalline lens. Which of the following best explains the functions of the lens? A. The lens controls stimulation of the retina. B. The lens orchestrates eye movement. C. The lens focuses light rays on the retina. D. The lens magnifies small objects. Answer: C. The lens focuses light rays on the retina. Rationale: The crystalline lens refracts (focuses) incoming light rays onto the retina; cataract opacity blurs this focus (Anatomy & Physiology; Brunner & Suddarth's). Pupil/iris controls light intake and extraocular muscles control movement, not the lens. 611. A client who has glaucoma is to have miotic eye drops instilled in both eyes. The nurse knows that the purpose of the medication is to: A. Anesthetize the cornea B. Dilate the pupils C. Constrict the pupils D. Paralyze the muscles of accommodation Answer: C. Constrict the pupils Rationale: Miotics (e.g., pilocarpine) constrict the pupil, which widens the trabecular outflow and lowers intraocular pressure in glaucoma (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya EML ophthalmic drugs). 'Miosis' means pupillary constriction, the opposite of mydriasis/dilation. 612. A client with a severe corneal ulcer has an order for Gentamicin gtt. q 4 hours and Neomycin 1 gtt q 4 hours. Which of the following schedules should be used when administering the drops? A. Allow 5 minutes between the two medications. B. The medications may be used together. C. The medications should be separated by a cycloplegic drug. D. The medications should not be used in the same client. Answer: A. Allow 5 minutes between the two medications. Rationale: When two different eye drops are ordered, a waiting interval (about 5 minutes) is required so the first drop is not washed out before absorption (Kozier & Erb's Fundamentals of Nursing). They should not be instilled simultaneously. 613. The client with color blindness will most likely have problems distinguishing which of the following colors? A. Orange B. Violet C. Red D. White Answer: C. Red Rationale: The most common inherited color blindness is red-green deficiency, so red is the color most likely confused (Anatomy & Physiology of vision). Violet and orange are less commonly affected and white is not a hue. 614. The client with a pacemaker should be taught to: A. Report ankle edema B. Check his blood pressure daily C. Refrain from using a microwave oven D. Monitor his pulse rate Answer: D. Monitor his pulse rate Rationale: Pacemaker clients are taught to check their pulse daily and report a rate below the set threshold, which signals pacemaker malfunction (Brunner & Suddarth's). Modern microwaves are safe, so refraining from them is unnecessary. 615. The client with enuresis is being taught regarding bladder retraining. The nurse should advise the client to refrain from drinking after: A. 1900 B. 1200 C. 1000 D. 0700 Answer: A. 1900 Rationale: In bladder retraining for enuresis, fluids are restricted in the evening (after about 1900 hrs / 7 pm) to reduce night-time bladder filling, while daytime intake stays adequate (Kozier & Erb's Fundamentals of Nursing). Stopping fluids at midday would cause dehydration. 616. Which of the following diet instructions should be given to the client with recurring urinary tract infections? A. Increase intake of meats. B. Avoid citrus fruits. C. Perform pericare with hydrogen peroxide. D. Drink a glass of cranberry juice every day. Answer: D. Drink a glass of cranberry juice every day. Rationale: Cranberry juice acidifies urine and inhibits bacterial adherence to the bladder wall, helping prevent recurrent UTIs (Brunner & Suddarth's). Citrus need not be avoided, and hydrogen peroxide pericare is inappropriate. 617. The physician has prescribed NPH insulin for a client with diabetes mellitus. Which statement indicates that the client knows when the peak action of the insulin occurs? A. "I will make sure I eat breakfast within 2 hours of taking my insulin." B. "I will need to carry candy or some form of sugar with me all the time." C. "I will eat a snack around three o'clock each afternoon." D. "I can save my dessert from supper for a bedtime snack." Answer: C. "I will eat a snack around three o'clock each afternoon." Rationale: NPH (intermediate-acting) insulin peaks roughly 6-12 hours after a morning dose, so a mid-afternoon snack covers the peak and prevents hypoglycemia (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya EML). Eating breakfast within 2 hours describes rapid/short-acting insulin. 618. A client with pneumocystis carinii pneumonia is receiving trimetrexate. The rationale for administering leucovorin calcium to a client receiving Methotrexate is to: A. Treat anemia. B. Create a synergistic effect. C. Increase the number of white blood cells. D. Reverse drug toxicity. Answer: D. Reverse drug toxicity. Rationale: Leucovorin (folinic acid) rescue counteracts the folate-antagonist toxicity of methotrexate/trimetrexate, protecting normal cells (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya EML). It is a rescue agent, not a synergistic or hematinic agent. 619. A client tells the nurse that she is allergic to eggs, dogs, rabbits, and chicken feathers. Which order should the nurse question? A. TB skin test B. Rubella vaccine C. ELISA test D. Chest x-ray Answer: B. Rubella vaccine Rationale: MMR/rubella vaccine is cultured in chick embryo cells, so a documented severe egg allergy warrants questioning the order (Brunner & Suddarth's; KEPI cautions). TB skin test, ELISA, and chest x-ray carry no egg-protein risk. 620. The physician has prescribed ranitidine (Zantac) for a client with erosive gastritis. The nurse should administer the medication: A. 30 minutes before meals B. With each meal C. In a single dose at bedtime D. 60 minutes after meals Answer: A. 30 minutes before meals Rationale: H2 antagonists such as ranitidine are best given before meals so the drug blocks the acid secretion stimulated by eating (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya EML). Single bedtime dosing does not cover mealtime acid surges as well. 621. A temporary colostomy is performed on the client with colon cancer. The nurse is aware that the proximal end of a double barrel colostomy: A. Is the opening on the client's left side B. Is the opening on the distal end on the client's left side C. Is the opening on the client's right side D. Is the opening on the distal right side Answer: C. Is the opening on the client's right side Rationale: In a double-barrel colostomy the proximal (functioning) stoma is on the client's right, following the direction of bowel flow from the ascending/transverse colon, while the distal non-functioning stoma is on the left (Brunner & Suddarth's). 622. While assessing the postpartal client, the nurse notes that the fundus is displaced to the right. Based on this finding, the nurse should: A. Ask the client to void B. Assess the blood pressure for hypotension C. Administer oxytocin D. Check for vaginal bleeding Answer: A. Ask the client to void Rationale: A fundus displaced to the right (and often above the umbilicus) indicates a full bladder; having the client void allows the uterus to recenter and contract, preventing atony (Myles Textbook for Midwives; Kenya MNH guidelines). Oxytocin is not first-line for a bladder-related displacement. 623. The physician has ordered an MRI for a client with an orthopedic ailment. An MRI should not be done if the client has: A. The need for oxygen therapy B. A history of claustrophobia C. A permanent pacemaker D. Sensory deafness Answer: C. A permanent pacemaker Rationale: MRI is contraindicated with most permanent pacemakers because the strong magnetic field can disrupt or damage the device (Brunner & Suddarth's). Claustrophobia and deafness can be accommodated and are not absolute contraindications. 624. A 6-month-old client is placed on strict bed rest following a hernia repair. Which toy is best suited to the client? A. Colorful crib mobile B. Hand-held electronic games C. Cars in a plastic container D. 30-piece jigsaw puzzle Answer: A. Colorful crib mobile Rationale: A colorful crib mobile suits a 6-month-old's developmental level (visual tracking) and is appropriate for strict bed rest (Basic Paediatric Protocols; growth & development principles). Electronic games and jigsaw puzzles are for older children. 625. The nurse is preparing to discharge a client with a long history of polio. The nurse should tell the client that: A. Taking a hot bath will decrease stiffness and spasticity. B. A schedule of strenuous exercise will improve muscle strength. C. Rest periods should be scheduled throughout the day. D. Visual disturbances can be corrected with prescription glasses. Answer: C. Rest periods should be scheduled throughout the day. Rationale: Clients with polio/post-polio syndrome fatigue easily, so scheduled rest periods conserve energy and protect weakened muscles (Brunner & Suddarth's). Strenuous exercise can worsen muscle weakness and is contraindicated. 626. A client on the postpartum unit has a proctoepisiotomy. The nurse should anticipate administering which medication? A. Dulcolax suppository B. Docusate sodium (Colace) C. Methyergonovine maleate (Methergine) D. Bromocriptine sulfate (Parlodel) Answer: B. Docusate sodium (Colace) Rationale: After a proctoepisiotomy (extending into the rectum), a stool softener such as docusate sodium prevents straining and protects the repair (Myles Textbook for Midwives). A stimulant Dulcolax suppository is avoided as it can traumatize the suture line. 627. A client with pancreatic cancer has an infusion of TPN (Total Parenteral Nutrition). The doctor has ordered for sliding-scale insulin. The most likely explanation for this order is: A. Total Parenteral Nutrition leads to negative nitrogen balance and elevated glucose levels. B. Total Parenteral Nutrition cannot be managed with oral hypoglycemics. C. Total Parenteral Nutrition is a high-glucose solution that often elevates the blood glucose levels. D. Total Parenteral Nutrition leads to further pancreatic disease. Answer: C. Total Parenteral Nutrition is a high-glucose solution that often elevates the blood glucose levels. Rationale: TPN is a hypertonic high-dextrose solution that commonly causes hyperglycemia, requiring sliding-scale insulin coverage (Brunner & Suddarth's). TPN actually promotes positive nitrogen balance, so option A is incorrect. 628. An adolescent primigravida who is 10 weeks pregnant attends the antepartal clinic for a first check-up. To develop a teaching plan, the nurse should initially assess: A. The client's knowledge of the signs of preterm labor B. The client's feelings about the pregnancy C. Whether the client was using a method of birth control D. The client's thought about future children Answer: B. The client's feelings about the pregnancy Rationale: For an adolescent primigravida, the nurse must first assess her feelings/acceptance of the pregnancy, as this shapes her receptiveness to any teaching plan (Myles Textbook for Midwives; Kenya focused antenatal care). Preterm-labor signs are taught later in pregnancy. 629. An obstetric client is admitted with dehydration. Which IV fluid would be most appropriate for the client? A. 0.45 normal saline B. Lactated Ringer's Rationale: Lactated Ringer's is an isotonic, balanced crystalloid ideal for restoring intravascular volume in dehydration (Kenya MOH fluid guidelines; Brunner & Suddarth's). 'Dextrose 1% in water' is not a standard preparation, and 0.45 NS is hypotonic. 630. The physician has ordered a thyroid scan to confirm the diagnosis. Before the procedure, the nurse should: A. Assess the client for allergies B. Bolus the client with IV fluid C. Tell the client he will be asleep D. Insert a urinary catheter Answer: A. Assess the client for allergies Rationale: A thyroid scan uses radioactive iodine tracer, so the nurse must assess for iodine/shellfish allergy before the procedure (Brunner & Suddarth's). Sedation, IV bolus, and catheterization are not routinely required. 631. The physician has ordered an injection of RhoGam for a client with blood type A negative. The nurse understands that RhoGam is given to: A. Provide immunity against Rh isoenzymes B. Prevent the formation of Rh antibodies C. Eliminate circulating Rh antibodies D. Convert the Rh factor from negative to positive Answer: B. Prevent the formation of Rh antibodies Rationale: RhoGam (anti-D immunoglobulin) provides passive immunity that suppresses the Rh-negative mother's active production of anti-Rh antibodies, protecting future pregnancies (Myles Textbook for Midwives; Kenya MNH guidelines). It does not convert the Rh factor or eliminate existing antibodies. 632. The nurse is caring for a client admitted to the emergency room after a fall. Stabilization with a plaster-of-Paris cast C. Surgery with Kirschner wire implantation D. A gauze dressing only Answer: B. Stabilization with a plaster-of-Paris cast Rationale: Simple closed fractures of the foot are typically immobilized with a plaster-of-Paris cast to allow bone healing (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya orthopaedic practice). A spica cast is for hip/thigh, and Kirschner wires are reserved for unstable/displaced fractures. 633. A client with bladder cancer is being treated with iridium seed implants. The nurse's discharge teaching should include telling the client to: A. Strain his urine B. Increase his fluid intake C. Report urinary frequency D. Avoid prolonged sitting Answer: B. Increase his fluid intake Rationale: After bladder iridium seed implants, increased fluid intake dilutes urine, reduces bladder irritation, and flushes the urinary tract (Brunner & Suddarth's oncology nursing). Straining urine is not indicated for internal implants. 634. Following a heart transplant, a client is started on medication to prevent organ rejection. Which category of medication prevents the formation of antibodies against the new organ? A. Antivirals B. Antibiotics C. Immunosuppressants D. Analgesics Answer: C. Immunosuppressants Rationale: Immunosuppressant drugs (e.g., cyclosporine, tacrolimus) suppress the immune response and prevent antibody-mediated rejection of the transplanted heart (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya EML). Antivirals and antibiotics treat infection, not rejection. 635. The nurse is preparing a client for cataract surgery. The nurse is aware that the procedure will use: A. Mydriatics to facilitate removal Rationale: Before cataract extraction, mydriatic (dilating) drops are instilled to widen the pupil and allow access to and removal of the lens (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya EML ophthalmic). Miotics constrict the pupil and would hinder surgery. 636. A client with Alzheimer's disease is awaiting placement in a skilled nursing facility. Placing simple signs to indicate the location of the bedroom, bathroom, and so on D. Alternating healthcare workers to prevent boredom Answer: C. Placing simple signs to indicate the location of the bedroom, bathroom, and so on Rationale: Simple orienting signs help the Alzheimer's client navigate and maintain independence and safety (Brunner & Suddarth's; mental health nursing). Mirrors can increase confusion/agitation and rotating caregivers reduces consistency. 637. A client with an abdominal cholecystectomy returns from surgery with a Jackson-Pratt drain. Provide for wound drainage Rationale: A Jackson-Pratt is a closed-suction drain whose main purpose is to remove serosanguineous fluid from the surgical wound bed, reducing collection and promoting healing (Kozier & Erb's; Brunner & Suddarth's). It does not keep the bile duct patent. 638. The nurse is performing an initial assessment of a newborn Caucasian male delivered at 32 weeks gestation. The nurse can expect to find the presence of: A.
