Head lag Rationale: A preterm infant at 32 weeks has immature neck muscle tone, so marked head lag is an expected finding (Myles Textbook for Midwives; Basic Paediatric Protocols). Scrotal rugae and abundant vernix develop later, closer to term. 639. The nurse is caring for a client admitted with multiple trauma. Fractures include the pelvis, femur, and ulna. Hematuria Rationale: With a pelvic fracture, hematuria signals possible bladder or urethral injury and must be reported immediately (Brunner & Suddarth's; Kenya trauma care). Muscle spasms and nausea are expected and less urgent findings. 640. An infant's Apgar score is 9 at 5 minutes. The nurse is aware that the most likely cause for the deduction of one point is: A. Rationale: Per Myles Textbook for Midwives, acrocyanosis (blue hands and feet) is the commonest reason a healthy newborn loses one Apgar point on colour, giving a score of 9; heart rate, tone and reflex are usually normal. 641. The primary reason for rapid continuous rewarming of the area affected by frostbite is to: A. Lessen the amount of cellular damage B. Prevent the formation of blisters C. Promote movement D. Prevent pain and discomfort Answer: A. Lessen the amount of cellular damage Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing, rapid continuous rewarming of frostbite in a warm water bath limits the extent of tissue and cellular destruction; the other options are secondary. 642. A client recently started on hemodialysis wants to know how the dialysis will take the place of his kidneys. The nurse's response is based on the knowledge that hemodialysis works by: A. Passing water through a dialyzing membrane B. Eliminating plasma proteins from the blood C. Lowering the pH by removing nonvolatile acids D. Filtering waste through a dialyzing membrane Answer: D. Filtering waste through a dialyzing membrane Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth's, hemodialysis removes nitrogenous waste and excess solutes by diffusion across a semipermeable dialyzing membrane; it does not remove plasma proteins and its purpose is waste filtration, not simply passing water. 643. During a home visit, a client with AIDS tells the nurse that he has been exposed to measles. Which action by the nurse is most appropriate? A. Administer an antibiotic B. Contact the physician for an order for immune globulin Rationale: Per Kenya HIV/AIDS and immunocompromised care guidelines and Brunner & Suddarth's, an immunosuppressed AIDS client exposed to measles should receive immune (immunoglobulin) prophylaxis; antibiotics and antivirals are not indicated for measles post-exposure protection. 644. A client who is admitted with an above-the-knee amputation tells the nurse that his foot hurts and itches. Which response by the nurse indicates understanding of phantom limb pain? A. "The pain will go away in a few days." B. "The pain is due to peripheral nervous system interruptions. I will get you some pain medication." C. "The pain is psychological because your foot is no longer there." D. "The pain and itching are due to the infection you had before the surgery." Answer: B. "The pain is due to peripheral nervous system interruptions. I will get you some pain medication." Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth's, phantom limb pain is a real physiologic phenomenon arising from severed peripheral nerve pathways and CNS reorganization, not psychological; it should be acknowledged and treated with analgesia. 645. A client with cancer of the pancreas has undergone a Whipple procedure. The nurse is aware that during the Whipple procedure, the doctor will remove the: A. Head of the pancreas B. The physician has ordered a minimal-bacteria diet for a client with neutropenia. The client should be taught to avoid eating: A. Fruits B. Salt C. Pepper D. Ketchup Answer: A. The nurse is assisting the physician with removal of a central venous catheter. To facilitate removal, the nurse should instruct the client to: A. Perform the Valsalva maneuver as the catheter is advanced Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth's, during central venous catheter removal the client performs the Valsalva maneuver (bear down/hold breath) to raise intrathoracic pressure and prevent air embolism as the catheter is withdrawn; the stem's wording 'advanced' reflects the removal procedure and the Valsalva timing is the key safety action. 648. A client has an order for streptokinase. Before administering the medication, the nurse should assess the client for: A. Allergies to pineapples and bananas B. The nurse is providing discharge teaching for the client with leukemia. The client should be told to avoid: A. Using oil- or cream-based soaps B. Flossing between the teeth C. The intake of salt D. An electric razor is actually recommended to prevent cuts. 650. The nurse is changing the ties of the client with a tracheotomy. The safest method of changing the tracheostomy ties is to: A. Rationale: Per Kozier & Erb's Fundamentals, the safest method when changing tracheostomy ties is to secure the new tie before removing the old one to prevent accidental decannulation. 651. The nurse is monitoring a client following a lung resection. The hourly output from the chest tube was 300mL. The nurse should give priority to: A. Turning the client to the left side B. Notifying the physician Rationale: Per Brunner & Suddarth's, chest tube drainage exceeding 100 mL/hr (here 300 mL) suggests active hemorrhage and is a priority to report to the physician immediately; milking the tube is contraindicated. 652. The infant is admitted to the unit with tetralogy of fallot. The nurse would anticipate an order for which medication? A. Digoxin B. Epinephrine C. Aminophylline D. Atropine Answer: A. The toddler is admitted with a cardiac anomaly. The nurse is aware that the infant with a ventricular septal defect will: A. Tire easily B. Grow normally C. Need more calories D. The nurse is monitoring a client with a history of stillborn infants. The nurse is aware that a nonstress test can be ordered for this client to: A. Determine lung maturity B. Measure the well-being of the fetus Rationale: Per Myles Textbook for Midwives, a nonstress test assesses fetal well-being through fetal heart rate accelerations with movement; while it detects fetal activity, its ordered purpose in a high-risk client is to evaluate overall fetal well-being. Source: NCK Paper 1 & 2 Combined Practice Sets (Type 1-4) 658. The physical manifestations of fetal alcohol syndrome include: A. cleft lip and palette. B. hepatomegaly, hypotonia, and microphthalmia. Per Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing. 660. The major pharmacologic action of Salbutamol is: A. decreasing airway reactivity. B. decreasing inflammation and airway obstruction. Effective supplementation of folate for prevention of neural tube defect is A. started at least 1 mo before conception, and continued through the first 2-3 mo of pregnancy B. started at least 3 mo before conception, to be stopped after positive pregnancy C. started after positive pregnancy test and continued through the first 2-3 mo of pregnancy. Answer: A. started at least 1 mo before conception, and continued through the first 2-3 mo of pregnancy Rationale: Folic acid for neural tube defect prevention should begin at least one month before conception and continue through the first trimester (first 2-3 months); per Kenya Maternal/Newborn and MOH antenatal guidelines. Neural tube closure occurs by 28 days, so periconceptional and early-pregnancy supplementation is required. 663. Expansion of the intravascular volume and increased intravascular pressure are the main causes of edema in A. lymphatic obstruction B. heart failure C. protein-losing enteropathy D. nephrotic syndrome Answer: B. heart failure Rationale: In heart failure, increased intravascular (venous/hydrostatic) volume and pressure drive fluid into interstitium causing oedema; per Brunner & Suddarth's Medical-Surgical Nursing. Lymphatic obstruction, protein-losing enteropathy and nephrotic syndrome cause oedema mainly via reduced oncotic pressure or lymphatic blockage, not raised intravascular volume/pressure. 664. Increased production of CO2 occurs in all the following EXCEPT A. fever B. emesis C. excess caloric intake D. high levels of physical activity Answer: B. emesis Rationale: Fever, excess caloric intake and high physical activity all raise metabolic rate and CO2 production; per Brunner & Suddarth acid-base physiology. Emesis (vomiting) does not increase CO2 production (it causes loss of gastric acid), so it is the EXCEPT answer. 665. Malignant hyperthermia is an acute hypermetabolic syndrome that is triggered by inhalational anesthetic agents and succinylcholine. Hypercarbia, arrhythmias and fever occur but appear later and are less specific as the initiating clue. 666. Cyanosis (unresponsive to oxygen) is a sign of poisoning with A. atropine B. amiodarone C. carbon monoxide D. vancomycin Answer: C. carbon monoxide Rationale: Cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen indicates that haemoglobin cannot carry/release oxygen, characteristic of carbon monoxide poisoning (and methaemoglobinaemia); per Brunner & Suddarth/toxicology. Atropine, amiodarone and vancomycin do not classically cause oxygen-refractory cyanosis. 667. The MOST common reason for a sick child visit is A. vomiting B. altered mental status C. respiratory distress D. fever Answer: D. fever Rationale: Fever is the single most common presenting complaint for sick child visits; per Kenya IMNCI and Basic Paediatric Protocols. Vomiting, altered mental status and respiratory distress are common but less frequent than fever as the chief complaint. 668. Major cause of neonatal mortality in full-term newborn is A. respiratory distress syndrome B. necrotizing enterocolitis C. bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) D. congenital anomalies Answer: D. congenital anomalies Rationale: In full-term newborns, congenital anomalies are the leading cause of neonatal mortality; per Kenya newborn care/Basic Paediatric Protocols. RDS, NEC and BPD predominate in preterm rather than term infants. 669. Common respiratory tract manifestations of neonatal bacterial infections is A. ethmoiditis B. empyema C. otitis media D. mastoiditis Answer: C. otitis media Rationale: Otitis media is a common upper respiratory tract manifestation of neonatal bacterial infection; per Basic Paediatric Protocols/neonatal texts. Ethmoiditis, empyema and mastoiditis are uncommon in neonates as presenting infections. ⚠ More than one defensible answer 670. Freedom of choice in one of the policies of the Family Planning Program. Scotch tape swab is done to check for which intestinal parasite? A. Ascaris B. . Pinworm C. . Hookworm D. Schistosoma Answer: B. . They are able to bring about a cure of the disease condition Your Answer : Rationale: Per Kenya National ARV Guidelines, ART suppresses viral replication, prolongs life, reduces opportunistic infections and lowers communicability, but does NOT cure HIV. The question asks which is NOT an expected action, so the correct answer is that ARVs cure the disease. 674. When assessing a 12 year old child with Wilm's tumor, the nurse should keep in mind that it most important to avoid which of the following? A. Measuring the child's chest circumference B. You are following a 6-year-old boy with autism, he is under structured psychosocial behavioral training program, there is frequent complains of aggression and self-injurious behavior.Of the following, the BEST medication to control his behavior is A. methylphenidate B. risperidone C. escitalopram D. amitriptyline Answer: B. risperidone Rationale: Risperidone is the FDA/WHO-approved atypical antipsychotic for irritability, aggression and self-injurious behaviour in autism (Kaplan & Sadock; standard paediatric pharmacology). Per Kenyan OSH regulations / community health nursing. ⚠ More than one defensible answer 242. The number of cases of Dengue fever usually increases towards the end of the rainy season. Bradycardia Rationale: Anticholinergic effects include tachycardia (not bradycardia), dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention and worsening of glaucoma; blockade of muscarinic receptors increases heart rate (pharmacology texts). 269. 22-year-old man started on a typical antipsychotic finds it difficult to sit still and has to move his legs constantly. The belief expressed by one of your clients that an alien is creating sores on his body with a knife is classified as: - A. Idea of reference B. Neologism C. Delusions D. D. The best approach for the mental health nurse to take when a client thinks his food is poisoned is to:- A. assure the client that all food served on the hospital is safe to eat. B. obtain an order for a tube feeding for the client. C. provide the client with food in unopened containers. D. tell the client that irrational thinking is detrimental to good health Answer: C. provide the client with food in unopened containers. Rationale: For a paranoid client fearing poisoned food, providing sealed/unopened containers reduces suspicion and promotes nutrition without arguing with the delusion (psychiatric nursing standard). Reassuring, arguing rationality, or tube feeding do not respect the therapeutic principle of not challenging delusions directly. 277. What nursing action would be most effective in changing the behavior of a child diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD):- A. Reward appropriate behavior B. Sedate the child for acting out C. Use aggressive punishment to control undesired behavior D. Use lengthy time out session Answer: A. Reward appropriate behavior Rationale: Positive reinforcement (rewarding appropriate behaviour) is the most effective behaviour-modification strategy for ADHD (psychiatric nursing). Sedation, aggressive punishment and lengthy time-outs are ineffective and inappropriate. 278. Which of the following nursing diagnoses would be considered the priority in planning care for the autistic child:- A. Risk for self-mutilation evidenced by banging head against wall B. Risk for self-mutilation evidenced by banging head against wall Rationale: Using Maslow/safety prioritisation, physical safety takes precedence, so risk for self-mutilation (head-banging) is the priority diagnosis for the autistic child (psychiatric nursing). Impaired interaction and communication, though characteristic, are not immediately life/safety threatening. 279. The child with conduct disorder will likely to demonstrate:- A. Distractibility B. Distractibility suggests ADHD and ritualistic behaviour suggests OCD/autism. 280. During psychiatric interview patient retains a constellation of ideas long after they have ceased to be appropriate.
